articles.title_orig: Brookings’ Michael O’Hanlon on China trip: I hope Trump holds the line on chips
articles.title_zh: Brookings’ Michael O’Hanlon on China trip: I hope Trump holds the line on chips
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held November 17th to 19th.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.

"The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears
articles.content_orig:
A group of workers who were dismissed from Rockstar Games were "caught red-handed" flouting contractual policies and obligations, an employment tribunal has heard.
The gaming giant behind Grand Theft Auto said it took action after staff discussed confidential information on a Discord server which had hundreds of members.
It came during the company's closing speech in a case brought by former employees who are claiming unfair dismissal for trade union activities. A judgement is due at a later date.
Representing 23 workers, the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB) said the former staff were penalised for discussing working conditions in a private online forum.
The conclusion of evidence comes ahead of the release of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 game on Thursday.
It is expected to break sales records when it is released. Pre-orders of the game are already though to be worth hundreds of millions of pounds.
Some 34 people are believed to have been dismissed from Rockstar North in October last year across the UK and Canada over what the company described as "the sharing of confidential company information".
The company's Rockstar North studio is in Holyrood Road, Edinburgh.
Thomas Cordrey, representing Rockstar, said employees made disparaging comments about the company on a semi-public Discord server and shared confidential information.
This included unreleased game features for Grand Theft Auto 6 and the timing of its release.
In his closing statement, he said moderators of the Discord server did not want to "over police" it and chose to "let the taps of disparagement and confidential information flow".
He added that the claimants "were caught red-handed" while Rockstar was under "enormous pressure" and on the "precipice of announcing further delays".
Cordrey said the alternative would have been 34 extended disciplinary hearings, all in the face of "inevitable dismissals for gross misconduct".
He urged Judge Lucy Wiseman to take into account the impact of going through these lengthier processes.
Cordrey also said the claimants did not appear apologetic about their conduct and described them as "blameworthy".
He told the tribunal: "This was a case of 'we know the policies, we know our employer would be opposed to the use of a semi-public Discord to disparage and breach confidentiality, but we did it anyway and we would do it again'.
"The reason why these individuals were dismissed was for that reason – flouting of contractual policies and obligations."
Managers were also said to be "vilified" in some posts on the server and the "most vitally protected resource" - Grand Theft Auto 6 - was discussed "liberally".
Cordrey added Rockstar was "obsessed by confidentiality".
He referred to evidence from the games developer's head of licensing, Jennifer Kolbe, who described being "shocked and appalled" at what was discovered on the Discord server in October last year.
He said union membership and activities had nothing to do with the dismissals.
In a statement, a spokesperson for Rockstar Games said: "Rockstar Games' position has been clear and consistent throughout.
"Individuals across the UK and Canada were dismissed for gross misconduct following the sharing of confidential company information, not because of alleged trade union membership or activity.
"The tribunal has heard our evidence and seen the facts, and the hearing has not yet concluded. We remain confident of a positive outcome."
The evidence concluded on Wednesday afternoon.
A timeframe for judgement was not given.

articles.title_orig: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year, Farm Bureau says
articles.title_zh: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year, Farm Bureau says
articles.content_orig:
For the first time since 2022, American shoppers will see an increase in the price of goods for Thanksgiving dinner. Results from the American Farm Bureau Federation's 41st annual Thanksgiving dinner cost survey indicate that the price of a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 people averages $58.63, up 6% from a year ago.
Over Four Decades of AFBF Thanksgiving Surveys
Each November, as millions of Americans prepare to gather with their family and friends to celebrate Thanksgiving, hundreds of volunteer shoppers from all 50 states and Puerto Rico participate in AFBF's annual Thanksgiving dinner cost survey. Every year since 1986, shoppers have reported prices for a standard list of items at their local grocery store for a variety of ingredients used to craft Thanksgiving favorites. Up until 2018, the survey included carrots, celery, cranberries, cubed stuffing, dinner rolls, frozen green peas, sweet potatoes, pumpkin pie mix, frozen pie crusts, whole milk, heavy whipping cream, and the ubiquitous American holiday staple: turkey. In 2018, AFBF added ham, frozen green beans and russet potatoes to better reflect the price of an all-American Thanksgiving meal.
While the overall cost of Thanksgiving dinner ticked upward in 2026, prices for several items included in the survey decreased slightly from 2025. A vegetable tray containing celery and carrots posted the largest percentage decline in this year's survey, with a 3.7% decrease compared to a year ago. In terms of absolute dollar changes, frozen pie crusts had the sharpest decrease, posting a decrease of 9 cents compared to a year ago. The survey bodes well for pumpkin pie enthusiasts, who will enjoy a lower overall cost for their beloved dessert despite an increase in the cost of pumpkin pie mix, as heavy whipping cream is also cheaper in 2026 compared to last year.
Higher Prices for Several Thanksgiving Favorites
The overall cost of a 10-person Thanksgiving dinner increased for 2026, largely fueled by increases in items key to the Turkey Day menu. The most notable increase for 2026 is the turkey itself, with the average price of a 16 pound frozen bird being $23.68, an increase of $2.38 (10%) from 2025. As discussed in a recent Farm Bureau Intel , strong demand and tight inventories have led to increased prices for turkey in 2026.
Apart from turkey, other widely featured Thanksgiving items increased in this year's survey. Grocery store prices for boneless ham, milk, dinner rolls, sweet potatoes, russet potatoes, frozen peas, frozen green beans, cranberries, and cubed stuffing (known in some regions as “dressing”) all increased in 2026.
Higher prices for these items aren't a complete surprise, as the effects of significant spikes in prices for critical inputs throughout the supply chain, like fuel for processing and transportation, have made their way to consumers. America's farmers and ranchers also face significant challenges, with record diesel costs, elevated fertilizer prices, increased labor expenses, and a bigger bill for items like rent and electricity — all of which hurt their ability to breakeven at the end of the year. However, unlike wholesalers and retailers, farmers aren’t able to pass those costs up the supply chain
Thanksgiving Dinner Prices Vary Across the Country
At an average of $61.57 for a 10-person classic Thanksgiving dinner, the Northeast has the highest cost. The Northeast's dinner basket cost is about 5% higher than the national average.  The average cost for a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 in the West and Midwest is closer to the national average, at $58.74 and $56.89, respectively. The South's average dinner cost is $54.33.
Some Shoppers May Find Great Deals
Despite the overall increase in the average cost of Thanksgiving dinner this year, some of our shoppers were able to find staggering deals on a variety of items, including turkey, which some shoppers reported finding  for as low as 69 cents per pound, nearly half the average nationwide price for a pound of turkey.  As Thanksgiving approaches, shoppers will look for deals on a variety of items to bring down the cost of their Thanksgiving dinner grocery list.
Higher Grocery Prices Do Not Mean Higher Farm Profits
Farm Bureau's 2026 Thanksgiving Dinner market basket survey indicates that Americans will pay more to feed family and friends this Thanksgiving. Nearly all items surveyed increased in price compared to 2025, with turkey, milk and cranberries posting some of the largest year-over-year percentage gains. However, higher grocery prices do not necessarily translate into better returns for America's farmers and ranchers.
Farmers and ranchers are largely price-takers, not price-makers, and receive only a small share of what consumers spend at the grocery store. USDA's Food Dollar Series estimates that less than 6 cents of every dollar spent on food goes back to the farm. Even when higher retail prices translate into increased farm revenue, rising production costs can quickly offset those gains. Elevated prices for critical inputs such as diesel, fertilizer and equipment continue to squeeze farm margins.
For example, this year's survey found that a 12-ounce bag of cranberries costs nearly 9% more than last year. That increase does not necessarily mean the Wisconsin cranberry farmer who grew them is receiving a higher price. Even if the farmer does capture some additional revenue, those earnings are needed to cover increased fertilizer, fuel and other production expenses.
As Americans gather around the Thanksgiving table, it's important to remember that higher food prices can place pressure on both consumers and the farmers who produce that food. Wherever and however you celebrate this Thanksgiving, take a moment to thank America's farmers and ranchers, who continue working through challenging economic conditions to provide the food, fuel and fiber we rely on every day.

articles.title_zh: Trump to meet Putin in China amid renewed push to end Ukraine war
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held Nov. 17 to 19.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang Scandal: Timeline That Led To His Resignation—And Potential Comeback
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang Scandal: Timeline That Led To His Resignation—And Potential Comeback
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night.
The announcement comes after Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO, should the board allow it. Huang abruptly resigned last week amid national security concerns and reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Jones said Nvidia’s board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent leader.
The company sought to reassure investors and offer clarity about its future in the third-quarter earnings report Tuesday evening, with Kress, saying Nvidia’s “roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.”
“Our ambition will not change, our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change,” Kress told investors, whose confidence in the company’s future has been badly shaken by the scandal , on the earnings call.
It’s the first financial picture investors are getting since the chipmaker was shaken last week by Huang’s resignation after three decades at the helm of the company he founded.
Nvidia more than doubled its quarterly revenue and profit from a year prior, and both figures beat Wall Street’s expectations.
Lies, spies and sex are just one part of the Nvidia story. The real stakes are much bigger
Nvidia’s earnings — the numbers and executives’ comments — have long been viewed as a bellwether for the larger AI industry, with Nvidia’s technology and funding at the heart of much of the boom. That’s especially true now with questions swirling about the industry’s future without Huang, its biggest cheerleader and dealmaker, at the helm.
Nvidia shares were coming off their worst week in 19 months heading into the report. The stock is down 16.7% since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair and Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, erasing $751 billion in market value. Since Nvidia shares hit their record high on October 6, they have dropped 35%, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market value.
Ahead of the report, Siebert Financial Chief Investment Officer Mark Malek wrote that it would be the “most important in the company’s history.”
Nvidia shares have dropped for four consecutive days since Huang resigned. Shares fell just 0.44% Tuesday. But shares moved higher in after-hours trading after the earnings release and analyst call, gaining roughly 5% as of 6:10 p.m. ET.
“The massive results, strong guidance and reassurance that the strategy Huang put in place remains firmly on track show that an orderly CEO transition does not necessarily have to dilute the company’s value,” Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com, said in emailed commentary following the release. He added that Nvidia’s growth train “can continue with or without Huang, provided the company makes the right call on leadership.”
Nvidia’s board said last week that Kress, the company’s CFO of 13 years, would serve as interim CEO as it considered internal and external candidates to permanently fill the role. Nvidia’s board also said Tuesday it had established a new national security and export control oversight committee to ensure the company is abiding by global trade regulations, and that it will strengthen its internal national security and compliance initiatives.
Some Nvidia employees, investors and other tech leaders had called on the board to reinstate Huang as CEO, pending the outcome of its investigation into his multiple reported extramarital affairs, including with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang , whom US officials suspect as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; and at least one direct subordinate at Nvidia.
Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided that his “return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America,” in his first public comment since resigning.
Jones said during Tuesday’s call that he would not take additional questions regarding Huang’s resignation or the company’s investigation, but that the board would “communicate further when appropriate.” Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company.
Meanwhile, Huang is set to testify on Capitol Hill on December 1. He is expected to face questions about his relationship with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s sales of chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which some US officials believed should have been labeled a national security risk.
Some US sources say that whether or not Alice Huang was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions.
Huang’s exit aside, concerns about whether the AI trade is a bubble about to burst, with valuations and infrastructure spending outpacing returns, had already begun to reach a fever pitch in recent months. Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN this week that he believes the AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election.
Nvidia’s Tuesday report indicates that, at least for now, the company’s growth continues to outpace Wall Street’s expectations.
The company posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% year-on-year. Profits reached more than $65 billion, up 105% year-on-year. Kress also said demand for the company’s next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology is “off to an explosive start,” with the tech already in use by customers such as Google, Microsoft and Oracle.
Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains strong, with a handful of the biggest AI and cloud companies expected to shell out more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures next year alone. But in the wake of Huang’s exit, investors have been more concerned with the company’s future business.
The report also comes after a blue wave in the US midterm elections ushered in a slate of newly elected leaders, many of whom campaigned on slowing or restricting data center development, which could dent Nvidia’s business.
Analysts with research firm IDC wrote in a report last week that the firm sees “near-term AI infrastructure demand and supply as largely locked in, so the harder questions,” like long-term bets on emerging technologies and the financing system that Jensen Huang sat in the center of , “sit further out.”
Nvidia said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to come in around $130 billion, plus or minus 3% — exceeding what Wall Street analysts had predicted, according to consensus estimates from FactSet.
Kress raised the company’s growth estimates for next year even higher from its already-ambitious targets, saying Nvidia’s revenue is expected to grow by 75% in fiscal 2028, up from 70% in the last earnings call.
Significant questions also remain about the future of Nvidia’s business in China, and potentially in Asia more broadly, as US officials react to the national security concerns surrounding the company.
Shipments of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China made up less than 1% of sales in its core data center business in the previous quarter . However, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15% of revenues when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.”

articles.title_orig: The Fed's next moves come into focus
articles.title_zh: The Fed's next moves come into focus
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Federal Reserve governor Chris Waller said Wednesday that if the central bank hikes interest rates by a quarter point next month, it will need to signal that the Fed will hike again by that much in January.
Otherwise, the Fed needs to raise rates by a jumbo half percentage point in December.
"People have argued, do you do 50 in December, nothing in January, or 25 in December, 25 in January," Waller said in an interview Wednesday on CNBC. "But when you do 25 now and you're going to do 25 in January, it only affects market pricing if you signal you're going to do it, and you give the markets a credible signal."
Waller said that if you leave the market guessing about a January rate increase, there won't be an effect on the market and, by extension, the economy.
"If you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets you're going in January, my view is then you have to go 50 in December," Waller said.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
That sounds a lot like forward guidance, which Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has sought to eliminate since taking the reins in May. Warsh has said that telegraphing future policy moves distorts market signals and boxes in policymakers.
But Warsh's philosophy hasn't quite taken hold, as other Fed members have continued to offer clues about the path ahead — which has also led to more questions and at times confusion in markets.
Without using the term explicitly, Waller argued Wednesday that the Fed would need to use forward guidance if it doesn't deliver a jumbo hike next month. He said the central bank could signal its next move either in the statement or at Warsh's press conference. He added that quarterly interest rate projections, which will be released in December, would be helpful this time because it's the end of the year and the projections would be for all of next year.
Waller said the Fed needs to be more aggressive because inflation is moving higher after remaining above the central bank's 2% goal for nearly six years.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Waller first hinted at a jumbo hike last week, saying ahead of the Consumer Price Index release, that if inflation came in higher than expected, stronger action would be needed.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2%.
On Wednesday, Waller said the Fed needs to take back the three rate cuts from last year and may need to do more to get inflation to come back down.
New York Federal Reserve president John Williams doesn't share that view.
Asked Tuesday during a Q&A with Axios in New York whether that latest inflation data calls for a supersize rate hike soon, Williams said, "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action."

articles.title_orig: El Salvador’s president confirms and celebrates attack on home of key Haitian gang leader
articles.title_zh: El Salvador’s president confirms and celebrates attack on home of key Haitian gang leader
articles.content_orig:
Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country.
On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”.
Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence.
The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti.
But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found.
“If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said.
That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay.
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge.
“The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday.
He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years.
“During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week.
The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead.
Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions.
Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations.
The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security.
Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials.
His heavy-handed approach has led to a sharp decline in crime but has also been widely condemned for human rights abuses.
Critics have warned that transplanting such tactics to Haiti could spark a backlash, leading to greater instability and risks to civilians.
They have also criticised the lack of long-term planning for El Salvador’s troop deployment; a sudden withdrawal, for instance, could worsen the situation for Haiti’s security forces.
Bukele is campaigning for a third term in El Salvador’s February presidential election, and analysts speculate his actions in Haiti could be used as a campaign tool to drum up support.
The Salvadoran deployment is the latest in a series of international interventions in Haiti.
Such foreign involvement is often controversial. The United States, for instance, has sent troops to Haiti on multiple occasions in the 20th century, occupying the country for decades and seizing control of its central bank.
More recently, a United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) arrived in Haiti in April, to help address the widespread gang violence.
Gangs control more than 80 percent of the capital region. The conflict has killed more than 22,000 people since 2022. UN reports attribute more than half of the deaths in the first nine months of the year to security operations, including the deaths of 300 civilians.
The UN also says almost 2,000 people have been displaced since the arrival of Salvadoran troops.
But Pelissier said Haiti’s government had not reported any civilian casualties in the latest operations, which he described as professional.
“The best to do is to avoid, as much as possible, human rights violations, and that’s what we are doing together,” the minister said.

articles.title_zh: Nasdaq rises in choppy trade as investors weigh Nvidia outlook, Anthropic IPO
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress gets an "A" for the financial performance and a "C" for the optics displayed on Tuesday's late-evening earnings call. New chair Harvey Jones — whom most Nvidia faithful have never heard of or from — gets a "C-" for his performance on the call.
The reality is Nvidia's leadership needs a better overall grade in the months ahead to sustainably win back market support.
Nvidia just put up another monster quarter, no doubt about it. Revenue and earnings easily topped expectations. Its outlook for the current quarter came in ahead of Wall Street estimates. Management pointed to approximately 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, up from the roughly 70% growth outlook then CEO Jensen Huang had previously discussed three months ago when he led the earnings call.
Let that sink in. Nvidia is talking about growing revenue at an extraordinary rate at a scale few companies in history have ever approached. Shares are up 2.5% on Wednesday in response.
There was more. The company cited a $2.5 trillion cloud backlog, expressed confidence that its next-generation chips will be released on schedule, and signaled that aggressive share repurchases will continue.
"FY28 underwritten as concern on near-term is largely addressed," Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley said.
But then there was the earnings call itself. And this is where things went astray.
This was Colette Kress's moment. The veteran Nvidia CFO is now Nvidia's interim CEO, stepping into a role that suddenly carries enormous weight following the leadership upheaval surrounding the disgraced Jensen Huang.
Yet the call felt strangely detached from the magnitude of what is happening inside the company.
Eight analysts asked questions. Not one mentioned Jensen's name. That was in part because Nvidia stonewalled them at the start of the call by saying it wouldn't answer any Jensen questions. This was tone deaf by Jones and Kress, and the analyst community did a horrible job of adhering to such bullshit from the world's most important stock.
Kress didn't mention his name either. Not once.
I found that remarkable. This is the man who founded Nvidia in 1993, helped build the products driving today's results, and became the face of the global AI revolution. The quarter being discussed was built on years of work under his intense leadership. The products shipping over the next 18 to 24 months will largely reflect that legacy too.
You don't have to turn an earnings call into a tribute to acknowledge reality.
Jones stumbled over remarks that sounded like he was reading from a fast-moving teleprompter. Maybe he is rusty at being in the public spotlight after years of yachting and home renovation work in his town of Nantucket, as this new profile would suggest .
Jones and Kress also leaned heavily on prepared remarks when addressing employees and the leadership transition. The message was essentially that employees remain committed and the company will take care of them. Fine. But investors deserve more than carefully rehearsed reassurances at a moment like this and in the wake of once-teflon Nvidia shares being down almost 30% in a month.
There was another important clue buried in the call: Kress sounded more measured about Nvidia's financial support for the so-called neocloud companies, including CoreWeave ( CRWV ). Nvidia has been an aggressive financial backer of parts of this AI ecosystem. Kress's comments suggested a more disciplined approach could be coming.
That matters. Nvidia needs customers with real businesses, real cash flows, and the ability to pay for the enormous amounts of computing infrastructure they are buying. The AI boom cannot run forever on circular financing and promises.
So here's where I land: The stock's initial positive reaction makes sense. The numbers were powerful. The demand outlook was explosive, as Kress characterized it. Nvidia is still an extraordinary business. But the company has a leadership problem to solve that quarterly revenue and profit beats cannot fix.
"We remain Sector Weight [rated], as uncertainty regarding who Jensen's successor will be likely keeps the stock range-bound," KeyBanc analyst John Vinh said.
Kress is a capable, experienced executive. She knows the numbers better than almost anyone. Nvidia clearly needs a permanent CEO who can combine technical credibility, strategic vision, and the kind of public-facing salesmanship that made Jensen Huang such a force.
You aren't going to find another Jensen. The assignment is to convince Wall Street that Nvidia's future doesn't depend on one person.
On earnings day, the numbers said yes. The earnings call didn't quite get there.

articles.title_orig: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
articles.title_zh: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
articles.content_orig:
The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rolled out a new proposed rule it said could save $90 billion over ten years through increased oversight and prevention of fraud and improper payments.
The Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare (CRUSH) proposed rule, shared late Monday, spans Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) and the Health Insurance Marketplace. It follows a request for information the administration circulated back in February. CMS it intends to conduct similar program integrity rulemaking “on an annual basis going forward.”
Among the highlights: stiffer provider screening and safeguards for Medicare enrollment, a new regulatory framework for reporting and returning self-identified Medicaid fee-for-service overpayments similar to those in other programs, and requirements that Medicaid managed care plans report beneficiary deaths or address changes within 30 days to help CMS better spot improper payments.
“When President Trump called upon the federal government to crush fraud, waste, and abuse , CMS got right to work, using every tool at its disposal to achieve historic savings,” CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, M.D., said in the agency’s announcement of the proposed rule. “CRUSH would build on those results by giving us stronger tools to prevent fraud, remove bad actors, and protect the Americans who rely on these programs. Whether criminals are billing Medicare for nonexistent canes and wheelchairs, fraudulently enrolling healthy seniors in Medicare-funded hospice care, or signing people up for Marketplace plans without their consent, the CRUSH proposed rule would give CMS stronger authority to stop these schemes and hold those responsible accountable.”
The additional guardrails are expected to cost the government about $378.5 million over the same 10-year period CMS expects to save nearly $90 billion, according to the proposed rule.
CMS, in its release and a lengthy fact sheet outlining the proposed changes, said it wants to update Medicare provisions to tighten Medicare Advantage (MA) Adjustment Data Validation audits so that it can better spot cases in which diagnoses are not supported by medical documentation, thereby bumping up risk scores and payments. It also wants to increase suspicious activity reporting requirements for MA organizations and Part D plan sponsors, require some MA plan providers and suppliers to also enroll in Original Medicare for credential verification and guard seniors from unsolicited outreach from medical supply companies.
In Medicaid and CHIP, the agency wants to make it easier for states to join in on suspected schemes while fleshing out their data collection and reporting. CMS also wants to add provider enrollment termination grounds similar to those in Medicare.
Within the marketplace, CMS said it wants to begin restricting access for agents and brokers with certain felony convictions or other healthcare program exclusions on their record. The agency is also looking to bolster its authority to suspend and terminate, and to do so more quickly.
“President Trump directed us to stop fraud, waste, and abuse, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is taking action to protect taxpayer dollars,” HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. said in the announcement. “CRUSH would give CMS stronger tools to block fraudulent payments, remove dishonest providers, and protect Americans from schemes that exploit their healthcare coverage.
Public comment on the proposed rule , which includes more potential changes and a breakdown of the expected savings and costs, will be open through Jan. 19, 2027.
The program integrity proposed rule landed the same day CMS released its estimates on improper payments during fiscal year 2026.
Improper payments are those that do not meet the agency’s program requirements, and can include overpayments or underpayments alike. They are not necessarily a measure of fraud, though “some improper payments may involve fraud or abuse” alongside administrative errors, CMS said.
In total, the agency outlined about $112.9 billion in estimated overpayments, an increase over the roughly $96.1 billion estimated for the prior fiscal year. That broke down into:
CMS noted that the estimates are tied to claims submitted from July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, a period “before many of CMS’ current crushing fraud initiatives were implemented.” Those and other efforts will begin appearing in next year’s improper payment data, it said.

articles.title_orig: Lenovo Legion Go Beam handheld leaks ahead of CES 2027
articles.title_zh: Lenovo Legion Go Beam handheld leaks ahead of CES 2027
articles.content_orig:
Lenovo is reportedly preparing a cheaper Legion Go handheld for CES 2027.
Windows Latest has published three images of an unannounced Lenovo gaming handheld reportedly called the Legion Go Beam. The device appears to be a simpler alternative to the Legion Go 2, with fixed controllers, thicker display bezels and fewer controls. Its specifications are unknown, but the design suggests Lenovo may be preparing a more affordable model.
The leaked device resembles the Legion Go S, including its controller layout and front-facing speakers. However, Lenovo appears to have removed the touchpad and adopted a different arrangement for the USB-C and microSD ports. The white chassis also features green accents around the analog sticks and along the bottom edge. Unlike the Legion Go 2, the Beam does not appear to support detachable controllers.
The more interesting question is what processor Lenovo plans to use. We have previously reported on Intel’s lower-end Panther Lake handheld processors, including an eight-core configuration with four Xe3 GPU cores. The latest information points to a design with eight Efficient cores, although an earlier configuration featured four Performance cores and four Low Power Efficient cores. Either could potentially serve as the basis for a cheaper handheld, provided Intel proceeds with these designs.
AMD is another possibility. We previously covered reports of the Ryzen Z3 series, which is said to use Zen 6 CPU cores and RDNA4m graphics. With CES 2027 approaching, AMD could announce its next generation of handheld processors. However, that does not necessarily mean Lenovo would use the latest chip in a budget device.
There is also the possibility that Lenovo could continue using an older AMD design. The Ryzen Z2 lineup already includes the Z2 Go and Z2 A, based on Zen 3+ and Zen 2 architectures, respectively. AMD could follow a similar strategy with its next generation, keeping older silicon available for more affordable systems. At this point, there is no evidence linking the Legion Go Beam to any specific processor.
Windows Latest suggests Lenovo could introduce the device at CES 2027, where the company is scheduled to hold its Tech World event on January 6. There is no confirmation of its launch date, pricing or operating system. Both Windows 11 and SteamOS remain possibilities, as Lenovo already offers both platforms with its handheld lineup.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia stock erases earnings pop as investors face life after Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: Nvidia stock erases earnings pop as investors face life after Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) bulls are getting hit with another reality check in a saga now in its second week.
That is, with no visionary Jensen Huang at the company, Nvidia is, well, just another chip company — one that's searching for somebody to fill a giant black leather jacket in the C-suite.
Shares of the tech giant reversed sharply on Wednesday from an initial positive post-earnings reaction. Nvidia stock is down about 3.5% at the time of this writing, reversing an almost 4% premarket pop.
"We view recently ousted founding CEO Jensen Huang as a singular leader who leaves impossible shoes to fill. Huang's departure creates a leadership vacuum which nature (and investors) abhor(s)," Oppenheimer analyst Rich Schafer said.
Schafer said he still has no price target on Nvidia's stock given the volatility. He removed his price target several days earlier.
Interim CEO Colette Kress made a solid case late Tuesday for staying in the interim CEO role for perhaps longer than Wall Street expects. At the bare minimum, she made the case that Nvidia isn't being led by a group of rookies undeserving of being in the room with a Huang-level exec.
The company's third quarter was solid , the outlook strong, and Kress came across as a steady hand driving the Nvidia rocketship.
For the third quarter, Nvidia posted adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street had expected earnings of $2.47 a share on revenue of $109.15 billion.
Nvidia expects fourth quarter revenue of $127.4 billion to $132.6 billion, comfortably above the $125.25 billion analysts were looking for.
The company said it sees fiscal year 2028 revenue growth of 75%, up from a prior estimate of 70% offered just three months ago.
But pros tell us new Nvidia chair Harvey Jones — who joined Kress on the earnings call — botched the messaging around the timeline of selecting a Huang replacement. Jones lacked a sense of urgency on bringing in a permanent top-notch exec — not what a nervous market wanted to hear from a chip company at the epicenter of the AI boom.
"I don't know that any internal candidate, though, is capable of running the whole company," Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg said on Sozzi Unleashed . "Jensen famously built the structure of the company around himself. Like he's the center of the wheel and all the things connect to him. And I don't think anyone internally has as complete a view of the company as Jensen does."

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 reviews say highly-anticipated game is a masterpiece
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 reviews say highly-anticipated game is a masterpiece
articles.content_orig:
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100 - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote , but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For The New York Times one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes , Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
The Washington Post said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg 's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.
The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.
There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.
Additional reporting by Jasmine Sandhar

articles.title_orig: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
articles.title_zh: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
articles.content_orig:
In today's how-could-things-get-worse-for-Microsoft news, it seems someone's GitHub org admin creds have been compromised
Microsoft’s official agent framework package hosted on PyPI has been hijacked and now installs info-stealing malware, multiple security research firms have discovered.
CEO Satya Nadella may be on stage trying to wow investors and customers at his company’s annual Ignite conference , but somewhere in the bowels of a building in Redmond his open source team is likely panicking at what appears to be unauthorized access to an administrator account on Microsoft’s Github organization.
The problem package is Microsoft’s agent-framework, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, researchers reported late yesterday and this morning . According to OX Security, version 1.26.1 was reverted to a safe version, but the attacker later uploaded 1.26.2 through Microsoft’s official PyPI publisher account, suggesting that, at least at the time of their report, the credentials hadn’t been locked down.
Safe to say, but if you find either version in your environment assume you have some account security work to do.
Microsoft agent-framework for Python boasts nearly 200,000 downloads a month and is used to build and deploy AI agents. As of those latest releases, it’s also being used to exfiltrate environment variables, credential files, and other secrets for Azure, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, and other sensitive developer services.
To make matters worse, the package never needs to be imported to do its dirty work – all it takes is a Python interpreter with the package installed to start up – the infected package still pulls the genuine 1.26.0 version of Microsoft’s agent-framework in order to keep itself running and looking legitimate, while in the background it gathers up credentials, encrypts them as a base64-encoded chunk of JSON, and sends them off to a webhook.site address hard coded into the malware.
It appears from researcher accounts that this is made to act fast, as the malware isn’t persistent and only runs as long as the malicious version of the agent-framework remains in a site-packages directory. What it does do, however, is not just look for credentials in the environment: It actually starts calling for new ones and collecting them, too.
In particular, the malware requests fresh identity tokens from GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure itself, which are exfiltrated to the same webhook site.
“That combination of passive theft and active token requests makes it especially dangerous in cloud build environments, because even short-lived tokens are useful when they're exfiltrated right away,” said researchers at OpenSourceMalware.
The agent-framework GitHub repo is offline as of writing. It’s been pointed out online that Microsoft’s repo for ONNX Runtime , an AI accelerator, is also offline. Other Microsoft repos remain available, and neither Microsoft nor security researchers have linked the ONNX repo’s pull to the malware campaign.
“We have made some repositories private while we investigate malicious content,” a Microsoft spokesperson told The Register. “Our priority is to protect customers and the broader ecosystem. We are working to review and will take further action as needed.”®

articles.title_orig: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Return to Titanium
articles.title_zh: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Return to Titanium
articles.content_orig:
Apple's rumored "iPhone 20 Pro" could return to titanium as part of a more rounded design, according to the leaker known as " Fixed Focus Digital ."
In a new post on Weibo , the leaker said the iPhone 20 Pro will adopt a titanium frame with a more rounded design. A frame made of titanium is reportedly currently in use on prototype devices during early engineering work. They described the design as somewhat similar to the iPhone Air , but substantially more rounded.
If the claim proves accurate, it would mark a return to titanium for the Pro lineup. Apple used titanium frames for the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro, before switching to an aluminum unibody design with the iPhone 17 Pro in 2025. Apple highlighted aluminum's thermal conductivity as part of that redesign, which also introduced a vapor chamber to improve sustained performance.
While the change was praised for its improved thermals, light weight, and distinctive design, some users missed the more premium look and feel of titanium, along with its superior resistance to damage. The latest report regards development hardware, so it is still open whether titanium will be used in the finished product, but it seems plausible. The ‌iPhone Air‌ and iPhone Duo continue to use titanium frames.
The leaker's comparison with the ‌iPhone Air‌ builds on earlier claims about how Apple is developing the anniversary models. Earlier this week, Fixed Focus Digital said the devices would use the same glass material as the ‌iPhone Air‌, reshaped with greater curvature along all four sides.
An illustration accompanying that post depicted curved front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished metal frame. In August, Fixed Focus Digital claimed that Apple had modified iPhone Air manufacturing equipment to produce the more rounded glass components.
That combination of curved glass and a narrow metal frame is consistent with Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman 's reporting that Apple is planning front and rear glass panels that curve into the sides around a thin metal band . Gurman said an earlier, more ambitious version that replaced even more metal with glass had been abandoned during development.
The latest claim suggests titanium could form that remaining band. Gurman described the planned changes as the biggest overhaul of the Pro line since the iPhone X.
The extent of the curvature may still be under consideration. The leaker "Ice Universe" today claimed that Apple is developing four models with two different designs , including two with flat glass and two with glass that curves along all four edges. Apple has reportedly explored the curved design for three years, reducing the more pronounced curvature of earlier versions.
The curved models are said to have borders measuring around 1mm, with the surrounding glass making them appear almost invisible when viewed head-on. Screen protector samples circulating online offer a physical illustration of that approach, showing rounded corners, shallow curves along all four edges, and very narrow borders.
Alongside the changes to the glass and frame, the displays could grow slightly. The leaker "Digital Chat Station" has claimed that the Pro and Pro Max models will feature 6.41-inch and 6.96-inch screens , respectively, while also describing a four-sided curved design intended to appear borderless.
Separately, Ice Universe suggested that the main camera could gain a sensor with logic circuitry manufactured using a 17-nanometer process , potentially enabling faster readout speeds and improved power efficiency. The device could also lose the Action button and feature the "A21 Pro" chip based on TSMC's enhanced 2nm process (N2P).
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027. Leakers have referred to the devices as the "iPhone 20 Pro," but Apple's actual naming plans are unknown.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia's Chinese whispers reach Indian-American executive Jay Puri
articles.title_zh: Nvidia's Chinese whispers reach Indian-American executive Jay Puri
articles.content_orig:
Another short-seller is betting against Nvidia over problems it sees with alleged ties to China.
Muddy Waters, the activist short-seller run by Carson Block, unveiled a bearish bet ahead of the chip giant's earnings on Tuesday .
The firm's report centers around an ongoing class action complaint filed in October in California against Super Micro Computer, a company that makes servers and other hardware for AI systems. The suit claims that an executive named Cenly Chen had knowledge of illicit sales of Nvidia chips to China.
Muddy Waters points to Chen and a potential connection to former Nvidia executive Ajay Puri. The two have been photographed together numerous times over the years, though neither Muddy Waters' report nor the lawsuit directly accuse Puri or Nvidia of any wrongdoing.
"A woman identified as Cenly Chen, referred to in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, has been photographed in public between 2024 to 2026 with Ajay K. Puri. Until this June, Mr. Puri was likely the third most senior executive at NVDA, behind only Jensen Huang and Colette Kress," the firm's report reads.
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Super Micro Computer issued the following statement regarding Muddy Waters' report to Business Insider:
"Cenly Chen did not manage Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers," a spokesperson said. "After 18 years at Supermicro, Ms. Chen voluntarily resigned in early 2026 to take the CEO role at ChronoScale."
Muddy Waters said that Super Micro Computer did not respond to requests to confirm if the woman photographed was the same Cenly Chen who held roles at the firm, including as chief growth officer and managing director.
Super Micro Computer has come under legal scrutiny in the past. In March 2026, one of its co-founders was part of a group arrested for illegally smuggling AI chip components into China.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
"In March this year, the U.S. indicted three individuals associated with SMCI, including a co-founder, for illegally selling at least approximately $2.5 billion of SMCI servers with NVDA GPUs to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company," the Muddy Waters report states.
It added that a former Super Micro Computer executive stated in the lawsuit that there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge of [SMCI's] illicit sales."
This is the first time that Muddy Waters has announced a short position against the AI leader. The claims in its report aren't framed as wrongdoing on Nvidia's part.
At a time when investors are still focused on the fallout from Huang's alleged ties to Chinese tech executive Alice Huang, Puri's potential connection to Chen could raise more negative speculation as the chip leader tries to get back on its feet.
Muddy Waters CEO Carson Block said that his call is not based on a view of Nvidia's fundamentals or valuation. He told Business Insider he viewed the report as "our best shot at trying to get the company to go on the record and discuss if they have any knowledge of any issues there."
Nvidia did not discuss any of the details in Muddy Waters' report during Tuesday's earnings call.
The firm's report follows a short bet earlier this year revealed by Culper Research , which flagged many of the details that ended up turning into scandals for Jensen Huang this month, including his ties to Alice Huang and Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed.

articles.title_orig: Ford starts U.S. battery cell production using Chinese tech amid geopolitical tensions
articles.title_zh: Ford starts U.S. battery cell production using Chinese tech amid geopolitical tensions
articles.content_orig:
MARSHALL, Mich. — Ford Motor has started producing battery cells in the U.S. for its next generation of electric vehicles using technologies licensed by Chinese battery giant CATL.
The automaker said Wednesday that cell production at a $3 billion plant in Marshall, Michigan — roughly 100 miles west of Detroit — started last month and the cells are now shipping out. They'll be used in prototypes for its Fathom small electric pickup truck , which CEO Jim Farley has touted as rivaling Tesla and Chinese competitors.
The production marks a milestone for the Detroit automaker and is the next step toward using lower-cost lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, battery cells in U.S. vehicles. The technology was created in the U.S. but commercialized largely in China.
The automaker's decision to make the batteries at the roughly 2 million-square-foot facility has been criticized by some lawmakers and U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over Ford's ties to CATL.
Alan Clarke, Ford's vice president of advanced development projects, said licensing the technology from CATL helped the automaker bring the low-cost battery chemistry to the U.S. as quickly as possible.
"If we want to get to being able to produce affordable EVs in the United States, we need to also do it the fastest way possible," Clarke said Tuesday during a tour of the facility. "CATL being the biggest in the world means that they're the best supplier to get us that technology and help us learn ourselves how to produce LFP cells."
The U.S. government has increased scrutiny of Chinese ties with U.S. companies even as President Donald Trump is meeting this week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
In September, Duffy sent a letter to Farley expressing "profound concern" about Ford's ties to Chinese companies that it believes could be detrimental to the Detroit carmaker and the U.S. automotive industry. The White House a day later followed up by commending the automaker for its domestic jobs and manufacturing.
Ford — the largest producer of U.S. vehicles — has routinely touted its American roots, jobs and manufacturing, especially as the Biden and Trump administrations have pushed to onshore and grow U.S. production.
Ford's battery plant in Marshall is expected to be capable of producing 40 battery cells a minute, equating to 20 gigawatt-hours annually for EVs and the company's energy storage business. That's down from initial plans of up to 40 gigawatt-hours annually amid an EV pullback by the automaker and broader industry.
Ford has said the production pace will help reduce battery costs and that the facility has room for additional capacity if needed.
The facility is highly automated, but Ford said it's still in the early stages of certifying its processes, as it plans to ramp up cell production next year before the expected launch of the Fathom pickup during the fourth quarter of 2027.

articles.title_orig: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
articles.title_zh: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
articles.content_orig:
Ukrainian soldiers spent weeks navigating a decommissioned, underground Soviet-era gas pipeline to sneak behind enemy lines and launch a surprise attack on Russian troops this autumn as part of an operation to prevent the invading forces from reaching the eastern city of Kupiansk, according to the Ukrainian unit involved.
The operation forced the soldiers to get past barricades laid by Russian forces — including the bodies of fallen troops —   and involved close-quarters combat inside the roughly three-foot-wide pipeline, Ukraine's military said.
"Operation Veles" was carried out by members of the Ukrainian National Guard's Khartiia Corps in the Kharkiv region within the last couple of months, according to a series of posts by the unit on social media. The unit said troops crawled and were pulled on wheeled carts some nine miles through the underground pipeline before emerging behind Russian positions.
The operation was part of a broader Ukrainian effort, more than four and a half years into Russia's full-scale invasion , to prevent the invading forces from advancing toward the front-line city of Kupiansk.
The unit's social media posts quoted soldiers saying they engaged in close combat with grenades and small arms inside the pipe, where the cramped space came with pooled freezing water and traces of natural gas lingering years after the pipeline was decommissioned. Some Ukrainian forces spent as long as a month underground during the operation, the Khartiia Corps said.
"They used electric winches to move through the pipe, and transported ammunition and equipment on small wheelbarrows," the unit said in one post. It called the conditions "extremely harsh," and noted that the troops "constantly moving on their knees caused injuries, and dirt clogged the mechanisms of their weapons and caused malfunctions."
Russian troops had laid obstacles in some sections of the pipeline, with Ukrainian soldiers saying that some of those barricades included the bodies of other Russian soldiers. The claims by the Ukrainian forces about the battle have not been independently verified by CBS News.
Russian authorities have acknowledged the operation, referring to a Ukrainian raid.
The Khartiia Corps has not confirmed any Ukrainian casualties, but at least one report on the battle, by Britain's Telegraph newspaper, mentioned Ukrainian forces recovering the body of a fallen comrade from inside an underground gas pipeline.
The pipeline offered a way for Ukrainian forces to conceal their movements in one of the most heavily monitored sectors of the nearly 1,000-mile front line that stretches from the far north to the far south of eastern Ukraine.
Both sides have sought to exploit underground infrastructure to evade increasingly sophisticated aerial surveillance in a conflict shaped by drone warfare. In September 2025, Russian forces similarly attempted to use sections of underground pipeline to move troops closer to Ukrainian positions around the northern outskirts of Kupiansk without being detected by drones.
Military analysts say operations like the underground pipeline assault highlight how the widespread use of drones in Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion, and Ukraine's defense, have transformed modern warfare. Both sides rely heavily on surveillance and attack drones to find and strike troops and hardware moving in the open.
As a result, even short movements above ground can expose soldiers to near real-time observation and attack.
While underground operations present their own dangers, including limited ventilation, restricted movement, navigational challenges and the risk of entrapment, soldiers involved in the Ukrainian mission suggested the hazards were outweighed by the dangers posed above ground, where they could have been spotted by Russian drones.
"It's damp, it's dark, it reeks. There are corpses lying around, but I felt safer there," one Khartiia Corps member, using the callsign "Sgt. Santa," was quoted as saying in a post by the unit.
The operation came ahead of what could prove a critical juncture in the war. President Trump, who campaigned on ending the war quickly, has pushed hard for Ukraine and Russia to agree to a peace deal. Kyiv and its European allies fear, however, that the White House appears to be offering Vladimir Putin and Russia too much — including the prospect of major energy deals, with no significant concessions in return,  while putting pressure on Ukraine to make major territorial concessions without any concrete security guarantees.
Ukraine says the operation in the gas pipeline helped stop Russian forces from gaining more ground near Kupiansk, a city that Ukrainian forces recaptured from Russia's invading troops in 2022.
Mariia  Kashchenko contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
articles.title_zh: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
articles.content_orig:
United Launch Alliance said Wednesday that the failure of its Vulcan rocket during a launch on Sunday was caused by inadequate fuel supply.
“ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the company said in a statement . “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.”
The new information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.
This represents an important revelation from ULA and will provide some major relief to different parts of the US aerospace community, particularly Blue Origin and NASA.
That’s because the BE-4 engine is also the bedrock of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This powerful rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that was later attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.
After this anomaly, Blue Origin retrofitted the main oxygen valve, including for Vulcan missions. Now it’s clear that this retrofit was not implicated in the Vulcan accident. With the preliminary Vulcan investigation having largely exonerated the BE-4 engine, Blue Origin can press ahead with its return-to-flight mission with New Glenn, which could occur as soon as January.
“Following the Vulcan anomaly, Blue Origin immediately worked alongside ULA to review flight data and support the investigation,” Blue Origin said in a statement Wednesday. “Together, we identified that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines. ULA is a valued partner, and we look forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.”
Amid a worsening US launch crunch, New Glenn offers the most tangible option for near-term relief for satellite operators, including Amazon Leo, which lost dozens of satellites on Sunday. The heavy-lift rocket has many commercial and government customers lined up for launch. NASA in particular is counting on the rocket to launch a number of lunar missions in the next two years, as well as play a significant role in landing humans on the Moon later this decade.
Also a relief to NASA will be confirmation that Vulcan’s upper stage, the Centaur V, did not contribute to the failure. NASA recently contracted with ULA to use the Centaur V as its new upper stage for the Space Launch System rocket, enabling future missions to the Moon.
For ULA, however, the latest update only brings more challenges.
Vulcan represents the company’s great hope to remain relevant in a US launch industry increasingly dominated by SpaceX and newer entrants such as Blue Origin. With Vulcan on the sidelines, other companies, such as Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and Stoke Space, could also elbow out the once all-powerful launch firm.
Although Sunday’s Vulcan flight, its fifth overall, was the first outright mission failure for the rocket, two previous launches also experienced problems. Those issues involved the nozzle of the solid rocket boosters. ULA has now spent three years trying to move the rocket out of its teething phase and into regular operations. A successful launch on Sunday could have set up at least a monthly launch cadence next year.
Now, the cash-strapped company must also contend with a new issue involving propellant management and complicated plumbing that feeds liquid oxygen and methane to the BE-4 engines. It will certainly be offline for several months.

articles.title_orig: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer has ‘parted ways’ with Sandfall
articles.title_zh: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer has ‘parted ways’ with Sandfall
articles.content_orig:
Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year . In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.
"No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told  Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.
"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors."
Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations."
"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry."
Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste" , and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.
We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise , and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

articles.content_orig:
Earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits . Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits.
Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks.
This is standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device.
Here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X :
I hit my Siri AI usage limit, it still works though, including complex questions pic.twitter.com/XYYNPMnSnn
In a follow-up post, Ben clarifies that complex questions did stop working shortly after posting. As expected though, basic requests continued to work as usual—they don’t have a usage limit.
One question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The company shares just two examples of something advanced:
But leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.”
Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”
It would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the company.
