articles.title_orig: NVIDIA GeForce driver bug may cause continuous SSD writes even at idle
articles.title_zh: NVIDIA GeForce driver bug may cause continuous SSD writes even at idle
articles.content_orig:
NVIDIA drivers 621.14 and 621.24 reportedly cause repeated SSD writes at idle.
Users are reporting excessive SSD write activity caused by NVIDIA GeForce drivers, just days after AMD released a fix for a similar problem. The issue reportedly affects the NVIDIA Display Container service, which may continuously write data to the system drive even when the PC is idle. Some users claim write activity reaching 30GB per hour.
According to reports collected by TroubleGrid and discussions on NVIDIA’s official forums, the process responsible is NVDisplay.Container.exe. The service repeatedly writes to a binary logging file named nvlog.nvlgstg , located in the NVIDIA Corporation directory under ProgramData. Rather than appending new information, the process reportedly rewrites the file, generating repeated disk operations.
Users have traced increased activity to GeForce driver 621.14, released on November 4. One comparison showed approximately 515MB of process-level writes during five minutes of idle time, compared with less than 2MB using driver 621.01. Another user reported more than 3GB in ten minutes, while a separate report involving driver 621.24 claims approximately 30GB per hour. These measurements represent reported process activity and do not necessarily correspond to the same amount of physical SSD writes.
It seems Nvidia GPU drivers also constantly write to your SSD by u/Remarkable_Fly_4276 in pcmasterrace
The problem may also affect systems with NVIDIA’s recording and overlay features disabled. Some users reported reduced disk activity after disabling ShadowPlay-related features, while others continued experiencing the issue. Similar complaints about NVIDIA’s background logging date back several years, suggesting the behavior itself is not entirely new.
Affected users can check disk activity through Windows Resource Monitor by opening the Disk tab and looking for NVDisplay.Container.exe. Some users have temporarily reduced writes by stopping NVIDIA Display Container LS, deleting the affected log file and restarting the service. Others report that reverting to driver 621.01 resolves the problem. Disabling the service permanently can interfere with NVIDIA Control Panel and NVIDIA App functionality.
AMD recently addressed excessive system drive writes with Adrenalin 26.11.1, released on November 12. NVIDIA has not publicly acknowledged the current reports, and its latest 621.24 driver release notes do not list the issue.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
articles.title_zh: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night.
The announcement comes after Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO, should the board allow it. Huang abruptly resigned last week amid national security concerns and reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Jones said Nvidia’s board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent leader.
The company sought to reassure investors and offer clarity about its future in the third-quarter earnings report Tuesday evening, with Kress, saying Nvidia’s “roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.”
“Our ambition will not change, our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change,” Kress told investors, whose confidence in the company’s future has been badly shaken by the scandal , on the earnings call.
It’s the first financial picture investors are getting since the chipmaker was shaken last week by Huang’s resignation after three decades at the helm of the company he founded.
Nvidia more than doubled its quarterly revenue and profit from a year prior, and both figures beat Wall Street’s expectations.
Lies, spies and sex are just one part of the Nvidia story. The real stakes are much bigger
Nvidia’s earnings — the numbers and executives’ comments — have long been viewed as a bellwether for the larger AI industry, with Nvidia’s technology and funding at the heart of much of the boom. That’s especially true now with questions swirling about the industry’s future without Huang, its biggest cheerleader and dealmaker, at the helm.
Nvidia shares were coming off their worst week in 19 months heading into the report. The stock is down 16.7% since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair and Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, erasing $751 billion in market value. Since Nvidia shares hit their record high on October 6, they have dropped 35%, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market value.
Ahead of the report, Siebert Financial Chief Investment Officer Mark Malek wrote that it would be the “most important in the company’s history.”
Nvidia shares have dropped for four consecutive days since Huang resigned. Shares fell just 0.44% Tuesday. But shares moved higher in after-hours trading after the earnings release and analyst call, gaining roughly 5% as of 6:10 p.m. ET.
“The massive results, strong guidance and reassurance that the strategy Huang put in place remains firmly on track show that an orderly CEO transition does not necessarily have to dilute the company’s value,” Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com, said in emailed commentary following the release. He added that Nvidia’s growth train “can continue with or without Huang, provided the company makes the right call on leadership.”
Nvidia’s board said last week that Kress, the company’s CFO of 13 years, would serve as interim CEO as it considered internal and external candidates to permanently fill the role. Nvidia’s board also said Tuesday it had established a new national security and export control oversight committee to ensure the company is abiding by global trade regulations, and that it will strengthen its internal national security and compliance initiatives.
Some Nvidia employees, investors and other tech leaders had called on the board to reinstate Huang as CEO, pending the outcome of its investigation into his multiple reported extramarital affairs, including with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang , whom US officials suspect as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; and at least one direct subordinate at Nvidia.
Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided that his “return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America,” in his first public comment since resigning.
Jones said during Tuesday’s call that he would not take additional questions regarding Huang’s resignation or the company’s investigation, but that the board would “communicate further when appropriate.” Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company.
Meanwhile, Huang is set to testify on Capitol Hill on December 1. He is expected to face questions about his relationship with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s sales of chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which some US officials believed should have been labeled a national security risk.
Some US sources say that whether or not Alice Huang was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions.
Huang’s exit aside, concerns about whether the AI trade is a bubble about to burst, with valuations and infrastructure spending outpacing returns, had already begun to reach a fever pitch in recent months. Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN this week that he believes the AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election.
Nvidia’s Tuesday report indicates that, at least for now, the company’s growth continues to outpace Wall Street’s expectations.
The company posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% year-on-year. Profits reached more than $65 billion, up 105% year-on-year. Kress also said demand for the company’s next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology is “off to an explosive start,” with the tech already in use by customers such as Google, Microsoft and Oracle.
Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains strong, with a handful of the biggest AI and cloud companies expected to shell out more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures next year alone. But in the wake of Huang’s exit, investors have been more concerned with the company’s future business.
The report also comes after a blue wave in the US midterm elections ushered in a slate of newly elected leaders, many of whom campaigned on slowing or restricting data center development, which could dent Nvidia’s business.
Analysts with research firm IDC wrote in a report last week that the firm sees “near-term AI infrastructure demand and supply as largely locked in, so the harder questions,” like long-term bets on emerging technologies and the financing system that Jensen Huang sat in the center of , “sit further out.”
Nvidia said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to come in around $130 billion, plus or minus 3% — exceeding what Wall Street analysts had predicted, according to consensus estimates from FactSet.
Kress raised the company’s growth estimates for next year even higher from its already-ambitious targets, saying Nvidia’s revenue is expected to grow by 75% in fiscal 2028, up from 70% in the last earnings call.
Significant questions also remain about the future of Nvidia’s business in China, and potentially in Asia more broadly, as US officials react to the national security concerns surrounding the company.
Shipments of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China made up less than 1% of sales in its core data center business in the previous quarter . However, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15% of revenues when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.”

articles.title_orig: Trump Says the U.S. Will “Catch” China on Rare Earths Within 10 Months - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.title_zh: Trump Says the U.S. Will “Catch” China on Rare Earths Within 10 Months - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin .
It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.
He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit . Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents.
A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.
“China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said.
After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags.
Xi’s gesture Wednesday most likely reflects a desire by him and his government to “show respect to Trump,” which they know he enjoys, William Yang, a senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, said in a post on X .
“It is likely also an attempt to uphold the positive rapport between Xi and Trump ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations in the coming months,” he said.
When Trump last visited China in May, he was greeted at the airport in Beijing by Vice President Han Zheng.
Putin, who has a close relationship with Xi and has met with him 50 times as of Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader when he arrived earlier at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport. Putin was instead met by Cai Qi, a close Xi adviser and member of the Politburo Standing Committee.
Xi has met with a number of world leaders, including Putin, as they gather in Shenzhen this week for a summit of Asia-Pacific economies.
Trump, Putin and Xi are holding an unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the summit.
Ahead of his bilateral meeting with Xi on Wednesday, Putin said he expected “great potential benefits” from the trilateral talks, which have sparked anxiety in places such as Ukraine, Iran and the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan, where officials worry the world’s three most powerful leaders could make decisions about their futures without consulting them.
In a briefing last week, a senior U.S. official said the trilateral meeting was unlikely to produce any sort of agreement, describing it as an “entry point” and “the first conversation.”
Jennifer Jett is the Asia Digital Editor for NBC News, based in Hong Kong.
Erin Tan is a news researcher in NBC News’s Beijing bureau.

articles.title_orig: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
articles.title_zh: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
articles.content_orig:
ABC News has sidelined the staffers behind a botched report about alleged investments tied to President Donald Trump’s children. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto)
ABC News quietly suspended staffers involved in the botched story last month suggesting impropriety in the Trump sons' business dealings, Fox News Digital has confirmed.
The Disney-owned network stirred controversy with its report headlined, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election," alleging that Anduril, the company investing in a new Baltimore shipyard, had ties to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump through 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm. The report claimed the firm had a "major stake" in Anduril, which was ultimately false.
ABC News raised eyebrows when it deleted the report without explanation after the story was called out on social media, then quietly republished a revised version of the report with an editor's note acknowledging the error.
GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR FCC PROBE OF ABC NEWS OVER TRUMP SONS-ANDURIL 'POLITICAL HIT JOB'
1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. serves as a partner, has considered legal action against ABC News. (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images)
The ordeal resulted in an internal probe to determine what went wrong. While two staffers behind the botched story were reprimanded and rumors they will be terminated swirl, an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "No one's employment status has changed."
ABC News declined further comment.
The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported that the two staffers were on "paid leave."
ABC News' original story wrote, "1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company."
"Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov , the official system for government contracting," the story continued. "The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one."
ABC NEWS QUIETLY REPUBLISHES GUTTED VERSION OF STORY ON TRUMP SONS IT HAD DELETED WITHOUT EXPLANATION
President Donald Trump and his son, Trump Organization Executive Vice President Eric Trump. (Brendan Moran/Sportsfile via Getty Images)
Alexa Henning, a spokesperson for 1789 Capital and a former chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, took to social media, insisting the company does not have a "major stake" in Anduril and blasting the "biased hit piece."
"Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning reacted at the time .
"Meaning the ‘investments’ mentioned were actually the total number raised for a funding round, that MANY companies contribute to," Henning continued. "Another thing that the reporter buried the lead on was that many of these companies have gotten government contracts during Biden AND Trump, which completely negates the assertion by ABC that Don Jr and Eric Trump are doing anything wrong."
VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM TIED TO DONALD TRUMP JR WEIGHS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST ABC NEWS OVER BOTCHED REPORT
ABC News then sparked confusion among critics when it deleted the entire story, only to republish an overhauled version of the story days later with the new headline reading, "New shipyard announced amid earlier Democratic concerns about potential conflicts of interest" while stressing to readers that Trump Jr. "is not involved in investment decisions."
"CORRECTION: A version of this story published on Oct. 7 contained errors in the description of certain company investments, government contracts and event chronologies," the editor's note read at the top of the article. "After subsequent reporting, this version contains corrected information and additional context regarding some of those investments, contracts and events."
Henning has said that nobody from ABC News asked 1789 for comment prior to the initial story being published and that an ABC News journalist "vigorously defended" the report before it was suddenly deleted. She also previously said the company was considering legal action against the Disney-owned news organization.
"This should be a cautionary tale for any other reporters who continue to traffic in this false narrative," Henning told Fox News Digital on Wednesday when asked if a lawsuit is still being considered.

articles.title_orig: Iran attacks US air base in Kuwait
articles.title_zh: Iran attacks US air base in Kuwait
articles.content_orig:
Iran has launched new attacks on its Gulf neighbours, targeting an airbase used by the United States military in Kuwait and carrying out several attacks on Bahrain after the US bombed Iran’s Qeshm Island.
Kuwait said it activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early September – and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack early on Wednesday, a day after the US attacked a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US said it carried out the strike in response to an Iranian attack on a US radar installation in Bahrain earlier on Tuesday.
Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s 5th Fleet, has experienced four Iranian attacks in six days, ending a weeks-long respite in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.
Iran said its recent attacks were in response to US drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.
The uptick in fighting raises the risk of a wider escalation towards the resumption of all-out conflict nearly nine months into the war, and complicates negotiations for a diplomatic solution, which have stagnated despite intensified mediation efforts from Qatar.
The Iranian attacks on the Gulf countries have drawn condemnation from across the region.
Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain “in the strongest terms” and denounced an attack on a tanker belonging to the United Arab Emirates.
The ministry said the kingdom rejects Iran’s disruption of shipping routes and urged a negotiated solution.
Arab League chief Nabil Fahmy said the repeated attacks on Arab countries reveal “a continuous escalation pattern that threatens to widen the circle of confrontation”. He also condemned the targeting of a ship belonging to the UAE’s national oil company, ADNOC, as it crossed the Strait of Hormuz.
Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, the Gulf Cooperation Council’s secretary-general, held Iran “responsible for this escalation and its repercussions on regional security”.
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry called the attacks “a dangerous escalation” that risks undermining diplomatic efforts. Kuwait and the UAE also condemned them.
Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry described the drone attacks as flagrant violations of its sovereignty and a direct threat to its security, Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi reported from Doha.
Basravi also said Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, warned that continued escalation without restraint from both the US and Iran makes a negotiated solution, or even continued dialogue, harder.
Meanwhile, Iran’s army chief, Major-General Amir Hatami, said the armed forces were “monitoring the enemy’s movements” after a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, the Fars news agency reported.
He said Iran’s response to any misstep by the US and its “backers” would be “even more crushing”.

articles.title_zh: Shelly’s new smart valve shuts off your home’s water before a leak becomes a flood
articles.content_orig:
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
After releasing a $28 leak sensor earlier this year that conveniently runs off a battery for two years, Shelly is announcing an accompanying smart valve you can install on your home’s main water line to automatically turn off the flow when one of those sensors detects a problem. The Shelly Neo Smart Water Valve is available now through the company’s online store for $499.99, plus the cost of installation if you don’t trust your plumbing skills. It’s not a cheap solution, but it’s cheaper than the fallout of a leak turning into a disaster.
The Neo Smart Water Valve is designed to be installed on a standard US 1-inch thread connection (the company plans to launch additional size options next year) and is made from brass so it’s safe to use on plumbing carrying drinking water. It has an IPX7 waterproof rating so the valve will keep working if flooding means it ends up submerged. However, the valve lacks a battery of its own and requires a connection to a power source through an included USB adapter cable. Connecting it to a waterproof power bank instead of an outlet may be the best approach to ensure it still works during a power outage.
The smart valve connects to other devices over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and is designed to integrate into existing smart home setups using webhooks, MQTT , or scripting for advanced users. In addition to shutting off the flow of water into your home in about 12 seconds, the valve also features an ultrasonic measurement system that tracks pressure, flow rate, your home’s consumption, and even the temperature of the water. Through the Shelly app, you can monitor all of that data in order to spot unusual usage patterns that could indicate a wasteful leak, or ensure the pressure doesn’t get high enough to damage pipes or appliances.

articles.content_orig:
Diehard GameCube fans can connect the controller to their original console, or use it with the Switch.
Diehard GameCube fans can connect the controller to their original console, or use it with the Switch.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64’s unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad’s centered analog stick. But with its new GC Bluetooth Gamepad , 8BitDo has done a much better job at staying faithful to the design of the Nintendo GameCube’s excellent controllers, including their unique button layout, thumbstick design, and shoulder buttons.
The 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad is available for preorder starting today for $49.99 in orange or purple and is expected to start shipping on December 10th. That’s much cheaper than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless remake of the GameCube controller, although 8BitDo’s version isn’t an exact copy of the original’s shape and ergonomics. If that’s important to you, and you have your GameCube’s original accessories on hand, you can still buy 8BitDo’s $25.98 upgrade kit, which is a cheaper way to make it compatible with modern consoles and devices.
8BitDo’s GameCube redux carries forward the original’s octagonal gates around the base of each thumbstick, making it well-suited to playing fighting games like Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . And while Nintendo continues to skip modern thumbstick technologies , the 8BitDo GC features both drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks and Hall effect linear triggers.
The controller connects to all versions of the Nintendo Switch over Bluetooth, as well as PCs or handheld consoles running Windows. It also comes with a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver for players who prefer a connection with lower latency, or you can connect it with a USB-C cable for the best possible performance.

articles.title_zh: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Russian Refineries Again as Fuel Shortages Spread Across at Least 8 Regions
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Ukraine reportedly struck the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory for the second time this month. The wider campaign has cut Russian crude processing by 30% and contributed to gasoline shortages and sales restrictions in at least eight regions.
Ukraine attacked two major oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory overnight on Wednesday, Nov. 18, marking the second strike on both facilities this month, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels and Russian media reports.
A large-scale drone attack targeted the Seversky District of the Krasnodar Territory.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Debris from the drones sparked fires at two industrial facilities, while fragments were found at nine other locations, including private residential yards and streets, the region’s operational headquarters reported. Four people were injured and are receiving medical attention.
The Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ identified the facilities as the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries. Sources cited by the Russian independent outlet Astra also confirmed fires at both sites.
The Afipsky refinery is one of the three largest in the Krasnodar Territory and among the five largest in southern Russia. It can process more than 7 million tons of crude oil annually, producing gasoline, diesel fuel, jet fuel, and other petroleum products. The facility is focused exclusively on exports.
The Wednesday strike was the eighth attack on the Afipsky refinery since the beginning of the year and the second this month. It was last targeted by Ukrainian drones on Nov. 6.
The Ilsky refinery is also among the three largest in the Krasnodar Territory, with an annual crude oil processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons. It produces gasoline, diesel, and other petroleum products.
The facility was last targeted on Monday, when, according to Ukraine’s General Staff, three atmospheric crude distillation units were hit.
The Russian defense ministry said its air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 184 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones between 8 p.m. Moscow time on Tuesday and 8 a.m. on Wednesday.
According to the ministry, the drones were intercepted over the Belgorod and Rostov regions, Krasnodar Krai, Crimea, and the Sea of Azov.
Ukraine’s General Staff later confirmed that two oil refineries had been struck.
“Ukraine’s Defense Forces launched an aerial attack on the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries – two key fuel suppliers in southern Russia,” the General Staff said in a statement published on Telegram.
As per the report, explosions and smoke were observed near the Ilsky refinery, where storage tanks were hit.
Preliminary information indicates that an oil processing unit was struck at the Afipsky refinery. The facility has an annual processing capacity of 6.25 million tons, accounting for more than 2% of Russia’s total oil refining capacity.
The General Staff said the two refineries have a combined annual processing capacity of approximately 13 million tons of oil.
“Located in the south, they serve as the shortest supply route for fuel to Russian forces at the front. Therefore, every fire at these facilities means less diesel and gasoline for the Russian army, and fewer ‘oil-rubles’ – funds the Russian aggressor uses to purchase missiles and Shahed drones,” the statement said.
“Exercising their right to self-defense, as guaranteed by Article 51 of the UN Charter, Ukraine’s Defense Forces continue to take systematic measures to compel Russia to cease its armed aggression against Ukraine,” it added.
Kyiv resumed its campaign against Russian oil refineries in late October. Over the past few weeks, Ukrainian forces have struck around 10 of Russia’s 35 refineries, including facilities in Novokuibyshevsk, Ryazan, Afipsky, Saratov, Yaroslavl, Omsk, Nizhny Novgorod, Ufa, and Kirishi.
The attacks have contributed to a sharp decline in Russia’s oil refining volumes. Refineries were processing approximately 700,000 metric tons (5 million barrels) of crude oil per day at the end of October, but that figure had fallen to around 500,000 tons per day by mid-November – a reduction of about 30%, according to informed sources cited by Reuters.
The drop in refining capacity has also contributed to fuel shortages at gas stations in at least eight Russian regions, The Moscow Times reported .
Restrictions on gasoline sales have been introduced in the Leningrad, Nizhny Novgorod, Arkhangelsk, Novosibirsk, and Penza regions, as well as in the republics of Karelia and Buryatia.
In Moscow, Rosneft gas stations have reinstated purchase limits: Motorists can buy no more than 50 liters (13 gallons) of fuel per vehicle, while sales in canisters are capped at 20 liters.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

articles.title_orig: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.title_zh: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held November 17th to 19th.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.
China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers
Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition
Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
Over the months I've spent following APEC's "China Year," one thing has become clear: The forum has given Beijing an opportunity to host the U.S., Japan and other member economies at a time when unresolved tensions might otherwise have made such gatherings difficult.
But even in a year defined by talks of U.S.-China "strategic stability," the APEC events have exposed the rifts and the shifting dynamics in global power. Those dynamics were on display for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
Several hundred attendees, from Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, arrived early for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
After waiting in silence for at least 10 minutes, the audience welcomed Xi in a distinctly modern way: by raising their smartphones to capture the moment. The applause was rather muted.
It was much the same at the more government-heavy welcome banquet that evening. So many attendees rushed to take their own photographs of Xi and other leaders entering the room that reporters' views were largely blocked.
Following Xi's morning speech, there was a lengthy intermission before Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took the stage.
"The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.
During the tea break that followed, attendees quickly resumed mingling. Some even brought coffee and snacks back into the room as Putin prepared to speak.
They listened as the Russian president talked about his country's economic resilience and claimed Europe was losing ground. As attendees headed to lunch, one thing stood out: Neither Trump nor any other G7 leader had taken the stage at the opening event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke later in the afternoon.
The most visible American presence during the morning session came from business leaders appearing in a promotional video ahead of Xi's speech.
And the absence of an American voice was perhaps even more noticeable at Wednesday evening's banquet.
Trump did not follow Xi with a toast of his own. This was the same famously outspoken president, who in a winding speech in Davos, had declared that the U.S. must get Greenland .
Yet on Wednesday night in China, Trump wasn't the one holding the microphone.

articles.title_orig: More details about Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone emerge - GSMArena.com news
articles.title_zh: More details about Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone emerge - GSMArena.com news
articles.content_orig:
Siddharth 18 November 2026
Apple is reportedly planning a major redesign for its 20th-anniversary iPhone 20 Pro lineup next year, with quad-curved displays and several other improvements. A new leak has now revealed more details about the upcoming models.
Tipster Ice Universe shared the latest details about the 20th-anniversary iPhones on X, claiming that Apple is developing four models for next year.
Two of the models will feature flat cover glass, while the other two will sport the much-rumored quad-curved design. Apple has reportedly been developing the new design for around three years, making several revisions along the way.
According to Ice Universe, early prototypes had deeper curves, which were later toned down. The tipster also claims that the quad-curved glass shown in a recently leaked video belonged to an early prototype.
The models with quad-curved glass are said to have 1mm bezels. However, the curvature is said to make them almost invisible when viewed straight on. Ice Universe also claims that industry insiders are more excited about the upcoming anniversary iPhones than the recently launched iPhone Duo .

articles.title_orig: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
articles.title_zh: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
articles.content_orig:
In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.
The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.
Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.
If they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18.5bn each.
So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?
In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.
He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.
Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track , and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.
Initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.
Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.
But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.
Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".
Dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.
She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.
Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.
She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.
The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.
Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.
He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.
Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.
He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".
Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.
Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.
Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.
He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.
Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.
Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.
He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.
His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.
Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.
But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.
Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.
He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.
The Canadian left the University of Toronto early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.
Sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.
McCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.
He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?
articles.title_zh: GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here - and that means we can finally share the full details of how the game performs on each console platform: base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S.
We've already covered GTA 6's visuals in detail , focusing on the top-end experience on PS5 Pro, but the game's performance and fidelity can vary significantly depending on your platform of choice. The PlayStation and Xbox releases use different upscalers, for example, while the PS5 Pro release adds extra ray tracing effects. The Series S version is perhaps the most interesting of all, as it has to cram an extraordinary visual burden onto the weakest current-gen hardware - and more or less pulls it off, despite some noticeable cutbacks.
This article compares the game on every platform based on over 100 hours of testing across all four versions by John and Oliver, focusing on image quality, visual features and performance.
First, let's touch on resolution. The game runs at 2560x1440 (1440p) resolution on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X, with no immediate signs of dynamic resolution scaling.
On PS5 Pro, this is upscaled to 4K using PSSR, the Pro's bespoke AI temporal upscaler. PS5 and Xbox Series X instead get a spatial upscale to 4K using Rockstar's in-house TAA. The game therefore doesn't use temporal upscaling - such as QSSR on PS5 or FSR on Series X - and appears visually softer as a result. However, the decision does make sense .
The Series S is the odd one out here, with an internal resolution of 720p, temporally upscaled to approximately 1080p using FSR 4. From what we understand, this is the first shipping game on Series consoles to use the new upscaler .
All platforms target a 30fps frame-rate, a rarity for a current-gen game, but given the huge scale and intense simulation elements, the design makes sense . There's no option for a 40fps or 60fps mode on any platform.
As an aside, Xbox consoles can run the game in a 120Hz VRR container as an OS-level feature, which allows for a slightly smoother experience. PlayStation users don't have a 120Hz option, and while you can force VRR on, the system-level VRR only operates above 48fps and doesn't support low frame-rate compensation, so this does nothing in a 30fps title.
In terms of performance, the PS5 Pro offers the smoothest experience, with a consistent 30fps experience through around 75 hours of standard play in our testing. However, it is possible to experience short drops to a minimum of 24fps when destroying vehicles with the grenade launcher, but the frame-rate tends to recover quickly.
The base PS5 and Series X use the same 30fps target, but hold it a little more loosely, often flicking between 30fps and the high 20s during traversal, combat and other more challenging scenes. Returning to the same vehicle destruction hotspot, the frame-rate remains in the mid-30s while the carnage is unfolding, and only recovers when we leave the area. Again, it's possible for frame-rates to dip into the low 20s at the worst case.
Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land.
Note that, distinct from frame-rate, the game featured some animation update rate unsteadiness in pre-release footage (and our early testing on Xbox Series consoles). Thankfully, this long-standing RAGE engine issue seems to have been fixed in patches prior to launch, and animations now play out with consistent frame pacing.
Finally, input lag is similar to other Rockstar 30fps titles, like Red Dead Redemption 2. We measured around 180ms of end-to-end camera movement latency on Series X, including a wireless controller and around 10ms of display latency. This didn't seem to change substantially across 60Hz, 120Hz and 120Hz VRR. This is similar to RDR 2 and GTA 5 Enhanced, though input response is perceptually a bit better in GTA 6.
While all versions of the game - PS5, PS5 Pro, Series X, Series S - use ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) and ray-traced reflections, only the PS5 Pro version additionally supports ray-traced shadows. On other platforms, less consistent shadow maps are used, though these do support variable penumbra and have a high-resolution appearance.
Note that the RT reflections on all consoles are part of a hybrid approach, with screen-space reflections (SSR) layered in.
The Series S version is surprisingly feature-complete compared to the PS5 and Series X versions, supporting strand-based hair and the two RT effects, but it does come with some cutbacks. Most notably, lighting is lower precision overall and RT reflections are softer, lower-res and sometimes miss details. Shadows also appear visually degraded, with lower resolution shadowmaps and some absent cutscene self-shadows.
Additionally, driving at high speed through the game world results in more noticeable pop-in. Other minor downgrades include muddier textures at oblique angles, lower-res volumetric clouds, flatter water, lower-res hair and facial hair, and lower resolution depth of field effects.
Despite these necessary cutbacks, due to the Series S console's more limited memory and cut-down GPU, the overall visual feature set is still similar to Xbox Series X and PS5. Thankfully, the full-fat CPU and SSD on the Series S mean that the scale and scope of Leonida isn't affected.
It's worth bearing in mind that the nature of the game make it hard to nail down absolutely every change, especially as John played only on PS5 and PS5 Pro, while Oliver played only on Xbox Series X and Series S. We'll have more direct cross-platform comparisons in future content.
In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through.
For more, why not read our full GTA 6 tech review ?

articles.title_orig: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.title_zh: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Bill Gurley , the venture capitalist behind an early bet on Uber ( UBER ), has an idea for how Google could slow Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) down: Give the AI away.
Gurley, a general partner at Benchmark, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google should use free AI to keep Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) from pulling away. Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday and begins trading Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT .
"If Google recognizes that Anthropic ... and OpenAI maybe are getting escape velocity away from them, it is the No. 1 thing they should go do ... bar none," he said.
Gurley calls it playing defense. Open-weight models, which anyone can download, run and change for free, keep one company from locking up a market. Google did it with Kubernetes "when they were worried about Amazon and AWS," he said, and with Android "when they were worried about Apple having a monopoly in phones."
The catch? "We're not seeing those actions from Google."
Free models already do most of the work. On OpenRouter, a marketplace developers use to reach hundreds of AI models, seven of the 10 most-used models last week came from Chinese labs and are free to download. DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash alone processed about 77 trillion tokens, the basic units of text that AI models read and write. That's more than the other nine combined.
Duolingo ( DUOL ) CEO Luis von Ahn told Yahoo Finance last week that open models cut the cost of each AI video call to less than a cent from about 30 cents. "The vast majority of our usage of AI will be in open-weight models pretty soon," he said.
The money flows the other way. Closed models handled 28% of OpenRouter's tokens in mid-September but collected 73% of the spending, according to its September report . Similarly, Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone accounted for about a fifth of phones sold in the second quarter but generated nearly half of revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.
Price is a big reason. Anthropic lists Claude Opus 5.5, its most-used model, at about 27 times what DeepSeek charges for its own. And while 39 companies sell DeepSeek's model on OpenRouter, nobody sells Claude Opus for less than Anthropic does. As Gurley put it, "The marginal price is going to equal marginal cost."
Gurley also called Anthropic's choice to write off model training costs right away, rather than over years, "pretty amazing," adding, "it's still profitable, really high gross margin."
"Anthropic — just reading through the S-1 — I think it's the most impressive business I've ever reviewed," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang on Friday.
OpenRouter tracks developers, not the ChatGPT or Claude apps. And Android cut both ways. It protected Google, but Apple kept collecting.
Gurley's worry is Washington. He said Anthropic's lobbying effort is "probably unprecedented for a company of their age or size," and he sees it as a push for regulatory capture , meaning rules shaped by the companies they govern. In AI, that could mean rules that favor closed labs over open models.
He still gives Anthropic its due. "It is remarkable what they've done," he said. "I tip my hat to them. I just wish they weren't lobbying so hard."

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.content_orig:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, panel Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify, Scott said. The agreements to appear voluntarily come as pressure builds on Capitol Hill to investigate Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led to his ouster at the chipmaker he founded.
"They both have agreed," Scott said. "We will hopefully have this done before Christmas."
Huang reached an agreement on Tuesday with the chairmen of three House committees for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 jointly before the three panels. Scott had asked Huang to appear publicly in the Senate.
A spokesperson for the banking committee did not immediately respond to questions about when Huang and Lutnick would testify. In initial letters to the pair, Scott requested Huang appear on Dec. 3 and Lutnick appear on Dec. 10.
Scott said the appearances will provide the committee with "more information about what they knew, when they knew it and why they didn't do something about it."
"Nvidia seemed to have fairly lax controls, and I want to know how much of the relationship with Alice [Huang] impacted Nvidia's unwillingness or inability, or frankly, just blindness to Megaspeed's providing access to China of the most advanced chipset," Scott said of Jensen Huang's testimony.
The outgoing banking committee chair also homed in on Lutnick, calling for answers as to why the commerce secretary did not act after being warned about Megaspeed — the Singaporean company where the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive. Nvidia sold its chips to Megaspeed, which U.S. investigators suspect of diverting them to China.
"They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the 'entity list,'" Scott said, referring to a Commerce Department list of companies the U.S. views as national security risks. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security "didn't do it, Howard didn't do it, we want to know why."
Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have been embroiled in an intra-administration battle as the fallout from the Huang affair grows. Bessent on CNBC on Friday appeared to blame Lutnick for a lack of action on Megaspeed.
"You will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said, referring to Commerce and noting his department has long supported imposing restrictions on Megaspeed.
A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment on Scott's announcement that he has agreed to appear.
Huang's upcoming appearances are likely just the start of the embattled former CEO's problems on Capitol Hill. Democrats will take control of Congress in January and have demanded sweeping investigations into the affair and Huang's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump .
The House Energy and Commerce Committee asked interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress for a briefing no later than Dec. 2 on the company's chip exports and information about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. The panel also asked Lutnick and a top deputy to appear to discuss chip export controls. The Wall Street Journal first reported the letters to Kress and Lutnick, and a committee spokesperson confirmed the report to CNBC.
— Megan Cassella and Ashlee Trujillo contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.title_zh: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.content_orig:
Copies of GTA 6 are beginning to arrive, with one difference spotted between the Xbox and PlayStation versions.
Grand Theft Auto VI ’s November 19 launch is almost finally upon us, with copies of the game already in the hands of many.
Preloads for digital copies of the game began on November 10 after Rockstar Games shifted the date forwards due to the title’s enormous file size .
For those who opted for code-in-a-box copies, preloads open today, on November 12.
Those who have a code-in-a-box copy in hand have taken to social media to reveal that the box features a double-sided fold-up poster, which is a nice touch.
One side features Lucia, with GTA VI ’s key art appearing on the other; the Grand Theft Auto franchise’s classic art style is used.
What has now been realised, however, is that those with an Xbox code-in-a-box copy are getting a slight downgrade compared to their PlayStation counterparts.
X (formerly Twitter) user GameRiot took to the site to share that “the GTA VI poster is actually smaller on Xbox compared to PS5”.
You can see in the video clip below that we’re not talking a couple of milimetres here.
There is likely a very good reason for this, as GameRiot points out, and that’s all down to case sizing.
While PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S physical cases are similarly sized, it appears that the area for posters, booklets, and such like within the Xbox case is slightly smaller.
Therefore, GTA VI ’s poster has been made smaller to fit accordingly, rather than this being any form of intentional slight to Xbox users.
It may feel that way amid Rockstar Games and PlayStation’s ongoing “plays best” marketing campaign that favours Sony’s console.
What isn’t abundantly clear yet is whether this difference in poster sizing is worldwide or whether this is unique to where GameRiot is based in the UK.
Grand Theft Auto fans are definitely seeing the humour in this latest spot.
“Cancelled my pre-order, unplayable,” joked BanksniO.
“They taking plays best on PS5 too seriously,” added vce_bby.
It’s a shame that Jason doesn’t get the chance to shine on the poster, unless he’s going to pop up elsewhere.
GameRiot did confirm that the PS5’s poster is roughly A3 sized while Xbox’s is understandably somewhat below A3 which could make the Xbox version difficult to frame, if that’s something you’re interested in.
READ MORE: GTA 6's first player ratings surface early via PlayStation Store, oops
It’s definitely been a busy week for GTA VI with an endless stream of marketing continuing to rollout.
Rockstar Games announced GTA VI : The Festival , a once-in-a-lifetime launch party based in Miami, Florida, plus Metacritic and Fandom have revealed a contest where you could win up to $500 in Visa gift cards simply by predicting GTA VI ’s Metacritic score .
We’ve also had confirmation that GTA VI will only run at 30fps , including on the PlayStation 5 Pro - something that’s ruffled a few feathers.
If you haven’t preloaded your game already, you may want to this weekend. GTA VI will be here before you know it.

articles.title_orig: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.title_zh: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.content_orig:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy
I n a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping , is basking in its neon glow.
On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.
The broader Apec summit , meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.
All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.
“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”
Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.
Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.
The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”
China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”
The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.
The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”
For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”

articles.title_orig: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar’s Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc
articles.title_zh: Knesset votes 66-52 to elect Yashar’s Matan Kahana as speaker, in boost to Eisenkot bloc
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s grip on power suffered a critical blow on Tuesday as parliament voted to elect a new speaker, giving the opposition greater control over the legislative agenda.
The Knesset elected Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party as its 26th speaker, replacing Amir Ohana, from Netanyahu’s Likud party. Kahana received the support of 66 lawmakers, according to the Knesset spokesperson.
Lawmakers voted separately on the candidates, rather than in a head-to-head ballot. Likud’s candidate, coalition whip Ofir Katz, received the support of 52 lawmakers in a separate vote.
The vote marks the first significant move by the Eisenkot-led bloc to set a new direction for the legislature since Netanyahu lost his Knesset majority in the October 27 elections. The prime minister and his coalition of right-wing and ultra-Orthodox parties won only 53 seats in the 120-seat parliament. The opposition holds 67 seats, including 48 across four Jewish parties and a record 19 for two Arab parties: the Joint List and Raam.
Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog earlier this month with forming the next government, has up to four and a half more weeks to replace Netanyahu, but his path to power remains difficult. However, his bloc now controls the Knesset plenum, key positions, and legislative agenda, and plans to use them to scrutinize and constrain Netanyahu’s caretaker government, which remains in office until it is replaced.
Eisenkot said Tuesday that Kahana’s appointment is a “proper democratic move which reflects the absolute majority who voted for change.”
Eisenkot’s bloc has already appointed interim chairs for key Knesset committees, including finance and defense, expanding oversight and control over the budget and strategic affairs. Avigdor Liberman, the leader of the opposition Yisrael Beitenu party now chairing the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, has already said he would summon all the security chiefs for briefings.
One of the opposition’s top legislative priorities is to undo judicial overhauls from Netanyahu’s outgoing coalition that sparked unprecedented nationwide protests in 2023. Critics of the overhaul said it weakened Israel’s democratic institutions and judicial oversight of the government.
Special committees have already been established to repeal a bill that changed how judges were selected and legislation that limits and weakens the attorney general. A separate committee was formed to undo a media regulation overhaul which expanded government control over the communications and news sector. Eisenkot’s bloc has also pledged to advance the establishment of a state commission of inquiry into the failures that led to the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, which Netanyahu has refused to investigate.
Netanyahu and his allies tried to block Kahana’s election and to delegitimize it as dependent on the support of the Arab parties, even though they themselves have repeatedly sought support from Arab lawmakers in parliament. During the vote, members of Netanyahu’s bloc shouted “shame” at each Arab lawmaker who voted in support of Kahana.
Likud condemned the outcome after the vote, calling it “a low point in the history of the Knesset” and saying Kahana had been elected with the votes of what it called “terror supporters.”
While Eisenkot and his allies have seized control of the Knesset, his plan to replace Netanyahu still faces significant obstacles. Eisenkot wanted to form what he calls a “national emergency government,” a minority government made of the four Jewish opposition parties, which together hold 48 seats. The Arab parties would stay out of the coalition but would guarantee a majority in the Knesset to keep the government from collapsing in exchange for various concessions.
But other leaders in Eisenkot’s bloc are pushing in different directions. Liberman has vetoed any government that relies on the Arab parties’ support and is pushing for talks with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), which have been traditionally allied with Netanyahu.
UTJ, the Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox party, declined to recommend Netanyahu for the premiership in the post-election consultations and has opened the door to informal talks with Eisenkot’s bloc. But it did not support Kahana in the vote for speaker of the Knesset, instead supporting Likud’s candidate. The second ultra-Orthodox party, Shas, remains loyal to Netanyahu, leaving Liberman’s strategy uncertain.
Another obstacle is former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who reportedly favors talks on a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud party over an alliance with the Arab or ultra-Orthodox parties. However, Netanyahu has conditioned any talks on him remaining prime minister, which Eisenkot has rejected, raising doubts Bennett’s vision can succeed.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.title_zh: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
Nvidia messaged chip buyers in recent months to caution that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services in the same way as physical hardware, potentially exposing both parties to legal risk, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The people asked not to be named while discussing private communications.
It also said that, for now, it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, the people said.
Separately, the Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia verbally told data-center clients to direct at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese customers under future contracts.
Regulators have had limited powers to control companies' access to those chips through cloud services hosted overseas.
RASA passed the House of Representatives in January but has not yet passed the Senate. Remote access to the chips has provoked the ire of President Donald Trump 's administration, which has sought to keep the chips out of China to maintain the U.S. lead in the AI race.
CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that Chinese lab Moonshot AI sought access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Europe. The Trump administration previously singled the company out, accusing it in July of accessing the chips through centers in East Asia.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia and BIS did not respond to a request for comment.
On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after Jensen Huang 's shock departure as CEO, amid reports of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China.
Bessent suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with export controls.
"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent told Fox News.
In an August securities filing , Nvidia said it sought to "strictly comply with all applicable export control regulators" but did not have "physical control of our products after sale" and relied on its customers' and partners' compliance programs.
Huang has been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.
